name: Programs and services of the Bangsamoro Government
note: Compiled from each office's Citizen's Charter, its website and the laws that created it. Requirements, fees and times are as the office published them; confirm with the office before you go.

offices.name: Office of the Chief Minister
offices.mandate: Supports the Chief Minister, the head of the Bangsamoro Government, in carrying out the Chief Minister's powers and functions. It also runs special programs for medical aid, relief and the Marawi rehabilitation.

contact.address: Bangsamoro Government Center, Rosary Heights VII, Cotabato City

programs.name: Ayudang Medikal mula sa Bangsamoro Government (AMBaG)
programs.summary: Helps poor and vulnerable patients pay hospital bills at partner hospitals.
programs.how: Bring the hospital papers to the AMBaG Office, 3rd Floor, Alnor Building 2, Sinsuat Avenue, Cotabato City.

programs.name: Tulong Alay sa Bangsamorong Nangangailangan (Project TABANG)
programs.summary: Gives relief goods to communities hit by disasters or conflict, and medicines, hygiene kits, food packs and free medical and dental services to isolated areas.
programs.how: Submit a request letter at the Project TABANG office on ND Avenue, Cotabato City.

programs.name: Marawi Rehabilitation Program (MRP)
programs.summary: Runs a mobile health clinic for displaced families and their host communities, and a lake ambulance and cadaver transport service in Lanao del Sur.
programs.how: Visit the mobile clinic with an ID, or call the MRP hotline for the lake ambulance.

programs.name: Bangsamoro Library and Archives
programs.summary: A public library at the Bangsamoro Government Center with reference materials, book loans, computer and internet use, and printing.
programs.how: Apply for a borrower's card with a valid ID and a membership form.

programs.name: Bangsamoro Liaison Office in Metro Manila
programs.summary: Gives referrals or endorsements for medical aid and 'Balik Probinsiya' help to poor or crisis-hit people from BARMM who are in Metro Manila.
programs.how: Submit a request letter and certificate of indigency to the liaison office.

programs.name: Community Monitoring and Actionable Complaints Tracking System (CM-ACTS)
programs.summary: Takes complaints from the public about BARMM infrastructure projects.
programs.how: Download the complaint form from the Contact Us page of bangsamoro.gov.ph.

services.name: Request for Medical Assistance (AMBaG)
services.summary: Cash help toward a hospital bill, paid through an endorsement letter to the hospital.
requirements: Request form (from the AMBaG desk officer)
Final hospital bill or charge slip (from the partner hospital)
services.where: AMBaG Office, 3rd Floor, Door No. 4, Alnor Building 2, Sinsuat Avenue, Cotabato City (0917-803-9295)

services.name: Request for Medical Assistance for billing above PhP10,000.00 (AMBaG)
services.summary: Medical help for hospital bills larger than PHP 10,000.
requirements: Final hospital bill or charge slip
Letter of request addressed to the Chief Minister
services.where: AMBaG Office, 3rd Floor, Door No. 4, Alnor Building 2, Sinsuat Avenue, Cotabato City

services.name: Mobile Health Care Clinic
services.summary: Free check-ups, basic dental and prenatal care, and medicines when available.
requirements: Government-issued ID or any document showing the patient's name
services.where: Marawi Rehabilitation Program - Program Management Office

services.name: Request for Emergency Care thru Lake Ambulance and for Post-Life Care for Deceased Persons thru Lake/Land Cadaver Transport
services.summary: Lake ambulance for patients and lake or land transport for the dead in Lanao del Sur, with priority for displaced persons.
requirements: Government-issued ID or any document showing the name of the patient or deceased, if available
Medical history records, if available (lake ambulance)
services.where: MRP-PMO, 1st Floor, Hanes Building, Panggao Saduc, Marawi City (hotline 0912-441-0991)

services.name: Request for Relief Assistance Program / Ayuda aLAy sa Bangsamoro (ALAB)
services.summary: Food packs, hygiene kits, kitchen wares and emergency kits for poor or disaster- and conflict-hit communities not yet helped by other agencies.
requirements: Request letter to the Project Manager stating the type and quantity of help and the number of affected communities, with a contact number
Photo of the affected area (for emergency requests)
Photocopy of the requester's valid ID
Valid ID of the beneficiary at release
services.time: 36 minutes to file; 3 days and 5 minutes for approval
services.where: Project TABANG Humanitarian Services Component, ND Avenue, Cotabato City ((064) 557-3914)

services.name: Health Services Assistance and Welfare Maintenance
services.summary: Medicines, hygiene kits, food packs, feeding programs and free medical and dental services for isolated areas named by health units.
requirements: Rural health units: endorsement letter from the Ministry of Health
Approval from the Health Unit Head or Project Manager
services.where: Project TABANG Health Component, ND Avenue, Poblacion III, Cotabato City

services.name: Request for Referral/Endorsement for Medical Assistance/'Balik Probinsiya' Assistance
services.summary: A referral letter for medical aid or help to return home, for poor or crisis-hit people from BARMM who are in Metro Manila.
requirements: Certificate of indigency or social case study report
Medical or clinical abstract (for medical aid)
Laboratory request or prescription (for medical aid)
services.where: Direct Community Service, Bangsamoro Liaison Office in Metro Manila

services.name: Application for Borrowers' Card
services.summary: A card that lets you borrow library books and materials.
requirements: Any valid ID (student, company, government, or a parent's or guardian's ID for minors)
services.where: Bangsamoro Library and Archives - Readers' Service

services.name: Request for Reservation or Rental of the Shariff Kabunsuan Cultural Complex (SKCC)
services.summary: Rent of the SKCC hall (up to 450 persons) for meetings, trainings, weddings, graduations and similar events.
requirements: Request or endorsement letter (2 original copies)
services.where: Administrative Management Services - General Services Division

services.name: Requests for an appointment or meeting with the Chief Minister
services.summary: Sets up a meeting or courtesy call with the Chief Minister.
requirements: Request letter addressed to the Chief Minister
services.where: Office of the Chief of Staff - Social Appointment Division

offices.name: Ministry of Basic, Higher and Technical Education
offices.mandate: The Bangsamoro Government ministry for education: basic education, college, technical-vocational training and the madaris (Islamic schools) system in BARMM.

programs.name: Access to Higher and Modern Education Scholarship Program (AHME-SP)
programs.summary: College scholarship; for school year 2026-2027 each scholar gets PHP 40,000 per semester (PHP 80,000 a year). It prioritizes former combatants, their children, orphans and surviving spouses.
programs.how: Apply online through the AHME portal during the application window (the 7th cohort window, April 13 to May 13, 2026, is closed).

programs.name: AHME College Assistance Program (AHME-CAP)
programs.summary: Yearly grant for college students from low-income families to help with tuition and school costs; 1,540 students were covered for school year 2026-2027.

programs.name: Bangsamoro Scholarship Program for Technical-Vocational Education and Training (BSP-TVET)
programs.summary: Free tech-voc training in courses such as Cookery NC II, Carpentry NC II, Driving NC II and Computer System Servicing NC II, run by MBHTE-TESD.

programs.name: Regional Manpower Development Center (RMDC) free skills training
programs.summary: Free tech-voc training for people aged 15 and up; trainees get a training certificate, a uniform, a PHP 180 daily allowance and referral to partner companies for on-the-job training.

programs.name: Abot Kaalaman sa Pamilyang Bangsamoro (AKAP)
programs.summary: Learning centers in remote barangays with no school, teaching preschool to Grade 3; run with the Australian Government through the Pathways program.

sources.label: BARMM Official Website, AHME-SP 7th cohort article, 2026
BARMM Official Website, RMDC free tech-voc training article, 2025

offices.name: Ministry of Health
offices.mandate: Plans, carries out and coordinates health policies and programs in the region, and delivers and regulates health services to protect and restore people's health.

contact.address: Bangsamoro Government Center, Rosary Heights VII, Cotabato City 9600

programs.name: Bangsamoro Medical Scholarship Program (BMSP-TDIF)
programs.summary: Pays for students in medicine and other health courses at partner schools; scholars must return to serve their communities after graduating and passing the board exam.

programs.name: PuroKalusugan (PK)
programs.summary: Rural health units bring immunization, consultations, medicines and health talks to puroks in the Special Geographic Area, launched May 2026.

programs.name: Bangsamoro Surgical and Medical Outreach Program
programs.summary: Medical missions offering consultations, circumcision, minor and major operations, eye surgery and check-ups, and wheelchairs, canes and crutches.

programs.name: Health facility building and upgrading
programs.summary: Builds and equips barangay health stations and rural health units, renovates hospitals, and provides land and sea ambulances.

programs.name: Health promotion with an Islamic perspective
programs.summary: Health education modules on the 7 national priority areas, written with Islamic scholars for Bangsamoro communities.

sources.label: Bangsamoro Administrative Code (BAA 13), Ministry of Health mandate, 2020
BIO, MOH accomplishments at Kapihan sa Bagong Pilipinas, 2024
Manila Central University, MCU and MOH BARMM scholarship partnership, 2026
SunStar Zamboanga (private outlet, citing BIO), PuroKalusugan rollout, 2026

offices.name: Ministry of Social Services and Development
offices.mandate: Provides social welfare in the region, with focus on poor and vulnerable groups such as women, children, older persons, persons with disabilities, indigenous communities and displaced persons, especially during disasters and conflict.

contact.address: Bangsamoro Government Center, MSSD-BARMM, Gov. Gutierrez Ave., RH-7, Cotabato City

programs.name: Angat Bangsamoro: Kabataan Tungo sa Karunungan (ABaKa)
programs.summary: A once-a-year cash grant for students from poor families: PHP 2,000 (elementary), PHP 3,000 (high school), PHP 10,000 (college or vocational). 4Ps students are not eligible.
programs.how: Apply at an MSSD regional, provincial or municipal office with an ID, proof of enrollment and a barangay certificate of residency or indigency.

programs.name: Unlad Pamilyang Bangsamoro Program
programs.summary: Livelihood, skills training and a monthly rice subsidy for poor families, with possible college support and emergency medical aid.

programs.name: Bangsamoro Sagip Kabuhayan Program (BSK)
programs.summary: A one-time PHP 15,000 seed capital grant to start or grow a small business, for low-income and disaster-hit households.
programs.how: Usually by referral; submit a valid ID, a livelihood project proposal and a General Intake Sheet for assessment by the municipal or city social welfare officer.

programs.name: Dakilang Bangsamoro Program (DAKILA)
programs.summary: PHP 1,000 a month plus seminars, mental health support and referrals for poor solo parents.
programs.how: Solo parents are assessed by MSSD social workers.

programs.name: Kalinga Para sa May Kapansanan Program (KALINGA)
programs.summary: A PHP 500 monthly stipend for poor persons with severe disabilities.
programs.how: Applicants are assessed on how much difficulty they have in six areas (seeing, hearing, walking, remembering, self-care, communicating); a PWD ID or medical certificate may be required.

programs.name: Social Pension for Indigent Senior Citizens (SocPen)
programs.summary: A PHP 1,000 monthly stipend for poor senior citizens aged 60 and above with no pension and no regular income.
programs.how: Submit an application form and a copy of your OSCA ID (or birth certificate or other ID) through your barangay senior citizens association, OSCA, the city/municipal social welfare office or the local MSSD office.

programs.name: Free Birth Registration
programs.summary: Free on-site birth registration for poor, unregistered children aged 0 to 12 in covered areas, with priority for Sama-Bajau, Teduray and former combatants' families.

programs.name: Kupkop Program
programs.summary: Food, schooling and monthly cash support for orphaned, homeless and neglected children.

programs.name: Women Opportunities to Maternal Benefits (WOMB)
programs.summary: Support for poor pregnant women for a safe pregnancy, childbirth and newborn care.

programs.name: Sagip Paningin para kay Lolo at Lola
programs.summary: Free customized eyeglasses for poor older persons.

programs.name: Layag Bajau Program
programs.summary: Livelihood, education, health, nutrition and resettlement support for Badjau families.

programs.name: Emergency Relief Assistance (ERA) and Emergency Shelter Assistance (ESA)
programs.summary: Food, non-food items and temporary shelter for families displaced by disasters or conflict.

services.name: B-CARES Hospitalization Assistance
services.summary: Help with hospital bills for poor or crisis-hit individuals, after assessment by an MSSD social worker; doctors' fees are not covered.
requirements: Valid ID of the informant and the beneficiary
Doctor's justification if admitted to a private room
services.where: MSSD Crisis Intervention Unit, CNX Building 3, RH-8, Cotabato City, or the nearest MSSD provincial office

services.name: B-CARES Laboratories and Other Procedures
services.summary: Help with costs of laboratory tests and procedures such as dialysis, chemotherapy, CT scan and MRI.
requirements: Laboratory request with date, doctor's signature and license number
Valid ID of the informant and the beneficiary
For other procedures: hospital quotation and medical certificate
services.where: MSSD Crisis Intervention Unit, CNX Building 3, RH-8, Cotabato City, or the nearest MSSD provincial office

services.name: B-CARES Medical Assistive Device
services.summary: Provision of devices such as wheelchairs, prosthetics or hearing aids.
requirements: Price quotation of the device from a clinic or supplier
Valid ID of the informant and the beneficiary
services.where: MSSD Crisis Intervention Unit, CNX Building 3, RH-8, Cotabato City, or the nearest MSSD provincial office

services.name: B-CARES Burial Assistance
services.summary: Help with funeral costs and transport of remains; must be claimed within 30 days of death.
requirements: Certification from a tribal chieftain or imam (if there is no death certificate)
Valid ID of the informant and the beneficiary
services.where: MSSD Crisis Intervention Unit, CNX Building 3, RH-8, Cotabato City, or the nearest MSSD provincial office

services.name: B-CARES Medicine Assistance
services.summary: Medicines for poor or crisis-hit individuals, released through partner pharmacies.
requirements: Prescription with date, doctor's signature and license number (valid for 2 months)
Valid ID of the informant and the beneficiary
services.where: MSSD Crisis Intervention Unit, CNX Building 3, RH-8, Cotabato City, or the nearest MSSD provincial office

sources.label: MSSD, program pages (ABaKa, BSK, DAKILA, KALINGA, Social Pension, Free Birth Registration)

offices.name: Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Agrarian Reform
offices.mandate: Leads farm and fishery development, land distribution and secure land tenure for farmers and fisherfolk in the Bangsamoro, and works to keep food available and affordable.

contact.address: BARMM Compound, Gov. Gutierrez Ave., Cotabato City, 9600

charter.label: MAFAR, Citizen's Charter (posted as 2024 2nd Edition; document says updated as of January 2021)

programs.name: Basic Integration for Harmonized Intervention (BIHI)
programs.summary: A package of farm interventions matched to each location, with checks on who the beneficiaries are, aimed at cutting farmer poverty.

programs.name: Corn Program
programs.summary: Support for corn and cassava farmers: seed production, buffer stocks, organic farming, biological pest control, marketing help, farmer training, irrigation and farm machinery.

programs.name: High Value Crops Development Program (HVCDP)
programs.summary: Promotes growing, processing, marketing and distribution of high value crops under RA 7900.

programs.name: Organic Agriculture Program
programs.summary: Promotes organic farming for better farm income, health and environmental protection.

programs.name: Integrated and Sustainable Development for Aquaculture/Capture
programs.summary: Livelihood packages for fisherfolk groups and individuals, such as seaweed inputs, motorized boats with fish aggregating devices, fishing gear and fish cages; post-harvest equipment for women fisherfolk; buying stations, mini ice plants and cold storage.

programs.name: Land Distribution and Development for the Upliftment of Poor ARBs
programs.summary: Distributes private and government-owned farm land to qualified farmer beneficiaries, and gives agrarian reform beneficiaries (ARBs) support: organizing, business services, shared facilities, infrastructure and legal help.

programs.name: ARCCESS
programs.summary: Grants of shared facilities or farm equipment and machinery to qualified agrarian reform beneficiary organizations, with business coaching.

programs.name: Special Development Fund (MAFAR-SDF)
programs.summary: Farm infrastructure and inputs such as farm-to-market roads, solar-powered irrigation, fish cages and agri-fishery inputs for cooperatives.

programs.name: Philippine Rural Development Project (PRDP)
programs.summary: Farm-to-market roads, trading posts, warehouses and processing facilities for farming and fishing communities.

programs.name: Registry System for Basic Sectors in Agriculture (RSBSA)
programs.summary: The registry of farmers and fisherfolk; the RSBSA enrollment form is required for many MAFAR services.
programs.how: Download the RSBSA form from the MAFAR website and submit it to MAFAR.

services.name: Market Development (buyer and seller matching, trade fairs)
services.summary: Helps farmers and fisherfolk find buyers or suppliers and join trade fairs.
requirements: Buyer or seller matching form (given at the office)
services.where: Agribusiness and Marketing Assistance, Market Development Section

services.name: Agribusiness Promotion
services.summary: Advice on starting an agri-business (costs, licensing, credit) and a business plan template.

services.name: Request for Shipping Permit of Pet Dogs and Cats
services.summary: Permit to ship a pet dog or cat.

services.name: Request for Shipping Permit of Fighting Cocks
services.summary: Permit to ship fighting cocks.

services.name: Request on Animal Vaccination, Deworming and Other Veterinary Drugs
services.summary: Free animal vaccines, dewormers and veterinary drugs.
requirements: Request letter approved by the Minister
For vaccines: ice and an ice box

services.name: Request for Training on Fruits, Vegetables and Industrial Crops Production
services.summary: Training on growing fruits, vegetables and industrial crops.
requirements: Project proposal endorsed by the MAFAR municipal officer and provincial head
Request letter approved by the Minister

services.name: Request for Seed Buffer-Stocking for Rehabilitation
services.summary: Seeds for farmers whose crops were damaged.

services.name: Request for Technical Assistance
services.summary: Farm technical help from MAFAR staff.
requirements: Request letter approved by the Minister
services.time: Depends on staff availability and type of help needed

services.name: Request for Training Center Reservation
services.summary: Booking of MAFAR training center rooms and halls.
requirements: Request letter approved by the Minister and endorsed by the Center Manager
services.fee: PHP 120 per head (accommodation); PHP 2,500 per training (hall and equipment)

services.name: Distribution of Quality Seeds and Planting Materials
services.summary: Seeds and planting materials, free or for sale.
requirements: Request letter approved by the Minister and released order by the Center Manager
services.fee: Free, or a price that depends on the crop if for sale

services.name: Request for Organic Fertilizer/Vermicast
services.summary: Purchase of organic fertilizer or vermicast.
requirements: Request letter approved by the Minister and endorsed by the Center Manager

services.name: Request for Soil Laboratory Analysis
services.summary: Lab test of a soil sample.
requirements: Request letter approved by the Minister and endorsed by the Center Manager

services.name: Request for Trichogramma Cards
services.summary: Purchase of trichogramma cards.
requirements: Request letter approved by the Minister and endorsed by the Center Manager

services.name: Request for Fecalysis Laboratory
services.summary: Lab test of an animal fecal sample.
requirements: Request letter approved by the Minister and endorsed by the Center Manager

services.name: Request for Commercial Fishing Vessel / Gear License (CFVGL) and Gear Registration
services.summary: License for a commercial fishing vessel and its gear.
requirements: Regional BFAR application form for fishing vessel license
Grid map locator of the proposed fishing ground
Two 8x10 color photos of the vessel (port, starboard, name)
MARINA documents: Certificate of Vessel Registry, Certificate of Ownership, current Certificate of Inspection
Articles of incorporation and by-laws, or business name registration
services.fee: Depends on vessel gross tonnage (GT), from PHP 200 + PHP 2/GT for small vessels
services.time: 3 working days, 4 hours and 30 minutes, plus 1-4 days travel for field inspection depending on the province

services.name: Request for Fish-workers License
services.summary: License for fish workers.

services.name: Request for Certificate of Clearance to Commercial Fishing Vessels
services.summary: Clearance certificate for commercial fishing vessels.
services.fee: PHP 200 (small scale), PHP 400 (medium scale), PHP 600 (large scale)

services.name: Request for Fishpond Lease Agreement (FLA)
services.summary: Lease of public land for a fishpond.
requirements: Registration papers if the applicant is a group or company
DENR Forest Management Bureau certification that the area is under BFAR
Final requirements as listed in the charter
services.fee: Application fee PHP 2,000; cash bond PHP 100 per hectare; rental fee PHP 100 per hectare
services.time: 5 working days, 6 hours and 50 minutes, plus travel time for field inspection
services.where: Fisheries regulatory unit or Provincial Fishery Office

services.name: Request for Local Transport Permit (LTP) for In-Country Trans-boundary Movement of Live Aquatic Species, Processed, Frozen, Chilled and Dried Aquatic Products
services.summary: Permit to move fish and aquatic products within the country.
requirements: Applicable permits or certificates (such as aquatic wildlife permits, health certificate, vessel license, auxiliary invoice)
services.fee: See the relevant Fisheries Administrative Order
services.where: Quarantine Officer at the fishport or airport

services.name: Request of Issuance of HACCP/SSOP/GMP/GHP Certificates
services.summary: Food safety certificates for fish processing establishments after inspection.
requirements: Sanitary permit and business permit from the LGU

services.name: Request of Health Certificate for In-Country Trans-boundary Movement of Live Shrimps, Live Aquatic Species and Seaweeds for Aquaculture Purposes
services.summary: Health certificate after lab analysis of stock to be transported.

services.name: Request for Aquaculture Farm Registration
services.summary: Registration of a fish farm after inspection.
services.time: 6 days and 12 hours, plus 9 working days for lab exam and approval at BFAR Central Office and 2-4 days travel
services.where: Provincial Fishery Office or Regional BFAR office

services.name: Request for Fish Kill Investigation / Disease Surveillance
services.summary: Investigation and lab testing when fish die in large numbers.
services.time: 6 hours and 1 minute, plus 1-2 working days travel to the site

services.name: Request for Water Parameters Analysis
services.summary: Lab analysis of a water sample.

services.name: Issuance of Certified True Copies of Agrarian Law Implementation case documents
services.summary: Certified copies of case records, decisions, resolutions and orders in agrarian law cases.
requirements: Authorization letter if a representative is requesting

sources.label: MAFAR, Citizen's Charter (posted as 2024 2nd Edition; document says updated as of January 2021)

offices.name: Ministry of Public Works
offices.mandate: The Bangsamoro Government's engineering and construction arm: plans, designs, builds and maintains roads, bridges, flood control, water supply and other public works in the region.

contact.address: Bangsamoro Government Center (BGC), RH7, Gov. Gutierrez Avenue, Cotabato City

programs.name: Expanded Bangsamoro Advanced Road Mapping and Management (E-BARMM) System
programs.summary: Online platform for planning and monitoring public works projects, meant to give the public real-time information on government projects across the region.

programs.name: Flood mitigation, dredging and river widening
programs.summary: Uses ministry equipment to clear silt and debris from rivers and drainage channels in flood-prone towns.

programs.name: Farm-to-market roads
programs.summary: Builds roads linking farms, markets and schools, including Japan-funded roads in South Upi, Maguindanao del Sur.

programs.name: Heavy equipment for barangays
programs.summary: District engineering offices hand over equipment such as dump trucks to barangays for road clearing, disaster response and upkeep, funded by Members of Parliament.

offices.name: Ministry of the Interior and Local Government
offices.mandate: Supervises the region's local governments (provinces, cities, municipalities, barangays) and builds their capacity, including in peace and order, public safety and disaster preparedness.

programs.name: Support to Local Moral Governance (SLMG)
programs.summary: Funds barangay halls, public markets, terminals and other small infrastructure built by local governments, with MILG monitoring.
programs.how: LGUs sign a memorandum of agreement with MILG.

programs.name: Local Government Functional Appraisal Award (LoGFA)
programs.summary: Assesses how well LGUs function; top LGUs received PHP 200,000 each in 2020.

programs.name: Lupon Tagapamayapa Incentive Award (LTIA)
programs.summary: Cash awards for barangays with well-run village justice (Lupon) systems.

programs.name: Bangsamoro Barangay Development Plan (BBDP) 2026-2028
programs.summary: A common 3-year planning guide and handbook for barangays, first used in 55 pilot barangays.

offices.name: Ministry of Human Settlements and Development
offices.mandate: The lead agency for housing, human settlements and urban development in the Bangsamoro: it plans, sets policy, regulates and coordinates housing and land use, and works to provide affordable housing.

contact.address: MHSD-BARMM Regional Office, near COA Office, Bangsamoro Government Center, Rosary Heights VII, Cotabato City

charter.label: MHSD, Citizen's Charter Handbook, 1st edition, January 2025

programs.name: SALAM Homes (Bangsamoro Affordable Housing Project)
programs.summary: House-and-lot units (36 sq m house on a 100 sq m lot) in Barangay Semba, Datu Odin Sinsuat, financed by Pag-IBIG at PHP 850,000, payable up to 30 years, with monthly payments from PHP 5,500.
programs.how: For BARMM employees who are active Pag-IBIG members, including contractual and job order staff; start with the MHSD preliminary qualification for a Pag-IBIG housing loan.

programs.name: Resettlement Project (free housing units)
programs.summary: Free house, lot and land title for families in need; 1,707 units were completed as of September 15, 2025.
programs.how: Beneficiaries (former MILF and MNLF combatants, the poorest of the poor, victims of calamity or conflict, indigenous peoples, displaced persons) are identified and selected with partners such as LGUs.

services.name: Request for Technical Assistance
services.summary: Expert help on housing, urban development and land use plans (CLUP and zoning ordinance).
requirements: Letter stating the request, addressed to MHSD, with supporting documents if needed
services.where: Environment, Land Use and Urban Development Division (ELUUDD); Provincial Offices

services.name: Request for Technical Assistance as Resource Person/Facilitator
services.summary: MHSD staff as speakers or facilitators for technical learning activities.
requirements: Request letter with a brief description of the activity
services.where: ELUUDD; Monitoring and Evaluation Division; Policy division

services.name: Request for Technical Inputs (Technical Assistance on the Review and Approval Process of CLUP/ZO)
services.summary: Technical review of an LGU draft Comprehensive Land Use Plan and Zoning Ordinance.
services.where: Technical Regulatory Service; ELUUDD; Provincial Offices

services.name: Application for Zoning Certification
services.summary: Certifies that a project fits the land zoning, for towns without an approved land use plan or zoning ordinance.
requirements: Notarized application form for zoning certification
Vicinity map to scale with geographic coordinates
Original and 1 photocopy of TCT/OCT, other proof of ownership, or tax declaration
services.fee: PHP 216 (per schedule of fees); PHP 720 per hectare for land conversion
services.where: Technical Regulatory Service; ELUUDD; Provincial Offices

services.name: Application for Locational Clearance
services.summary: Clearance needed before a building permit, confirming the project fits the land use plan and zoning.
requirements: Photocopy of land title or other proof of ownership
Certified true copy of latest tax declaration
Vicinity map of existing land uses
Environmental Compliance Certificate or Certificate of Non-Coverage (MENRE)
services.time: 2 days, 2 hours and 35 minutes (excluding delays for nonconforming projects or added inspections)
services.where: Technical Regulatory Service; ELUUDD; Provincial Offices

services.name: Application for Preliminary Subdivision Development Plan (PSDP), Development Permit (DP), and Alteration Plan (AP)
services.summary: Permits for planning, developing or altering a subdivision project.
requirements: 3 sets of subdivision plan, vicinity map and survey plan
Certified true copies of TCT, tax declaration and ownership proofs
Subdivision development plan and civil/sanitary works design signed by licensed professionals
Other documents listed in the charter
services.time: 18 days, 3 hours and 20 minutes (excluding time for corrections or incomplete documents)
services.where: Policy Development, Coordination and Regulation Division (PDCRD)

services.name: Application for Certificate of Registration (CR) and License to Sell (LS)
services.summary: Registration and license needed before selling subdivision lots or condominium units to the public.
requirements: Certified true copy of TCT or OCT
Articles of incorporation, by-laws and latest SEC report
MAFAR conversion order or exemption clearance
Other plans and permits listed in the charter
services.fee: CR: PHP 420 (socialized) or PHP 720 (economic); LS: PHP 24 (socialized) or PHP 72 (economic) per saleable lot, plus PHP 3 per sq m of housing area; inspection fee PHP 1,500
services.time: 6 days, 16 hours and 10 minutes (excluding delays from incomplete documents)

services.name: Application for Certificate of Completion (COC) of Subdivision Projects
services.summary: Certifies a registered project was finished as approved, before turnover of roads, parks and open spaces.
requirements: Proof of TCTs of open spaces

services.name: Application for Registration of Real Estate Brokers, Salespersons, Business Firms, and Dealers
services.summary: Registration needed to sell subdivision lots or condominium units.
requirements: PRC certificate of registration and ID (brokers)
For salespersons: letter of engagement signed by an MHSD-registered dealer or broker
services.time: 6 days, 12 hours and 45 minutes (excluding applicant delays)

services.name: Application for Registration of Homeowners Associations
services.summary: Gives a homeowners or neighborhood association legal personality.
requirements: Notarized articles of incorporation signed by all incorporators
Undertaking to change the name if needed
List of members certified by the secretary
Other documents listed in the charter
services.time: 11 days, 4 hours and 15 minutes (excluding applicant delays)

services.name: Preliminary Qualification for Application of Housing Loan Through Pag-IBIG
services.summary: First step to apply for the ministry affordable housing program: checks whether you qualify for a Pag-IBIG housing loan.
